summary.text: This investigation aims to determine the conditions under which cool diffusion flames occur for propane, n-butane, and n-pentane in normal and inverse configurations, through spherical diffusion flame tests aboard the ISS.

geometry.text: Spherical diffusion flames; spherical porous burners are hypothesized.

pressure.text: A range of pressures is considered.

flow.text: A range of flow rates, with normal and inverse convection directions.

measurements.text: Cameras, radiometers, photomultiplier tubes, and thermocouples.

claims.text: The investigation aims to determine the conditions for which cool diffusion flames occur for propane, n-butane, and n-pentane, for normal and inverse flames.
The investigation hypothesizes that ISS testing can demonstrate, for the first time, steady-state cool diffusion flames on spherical porous burners and inverse cool diffusion flames.

limitations.text: The metadata states objectives, hypotheses and approach but no measured result, so no reported observation or finding is recorded.
This draft cites PSI metadata and no PDF text. The packet also includes official table passages whose findings have not been incorporated or reviewed.

modeling_resources.description: Candidate data for modeling: normal-flame and inverse-flame experimental tables from the ISS tests, measured with the listed instruments. No model is claimed.

evidence.excerpt: Determine the conditions for which cool diffusion flames occur for propane, n-butane, and n-pentane; normal and inverse flames
The hypotheses of this research are that testing aboard the ISS can demonstrate the following for the first time
Steady-state cool diffusion flames on spherical porous burners.
Perform spherical diffusion flame tests aboard the International Space Station.
Consider multiple fuels, a range of reactant dilutions, flow rates, and pressures for normal and inverse convection directions.
Observe the flames with a broad suite of cameras, radiometers, photomultiplier tubes, and thermocouples.
